hook.text: A compressed file leaks information about its contents through its size. Attackers have exploited this.

buildup.text: CRIME and BREACH attacks measured response sizes to guess encrypted web tokens one character at a time.

discovery.text: If a guessed character matches the token, compression shrinks the response. Size difference reveals the match.

twist.text: Compression and encryption are fundamentally at odds: compression finds patterns, encryption hides them.

climax.text: Modern web servers disabled compression on sensitive data. Security required sacrificing bandwidth savings.

punchline.text: File size can leak secrets. Compression has a dark side.

quiz.question: How did CRIME/BREACH attacks exploit compression?
options: By measuring size changes to guess secret tokens
